title: Sometimes you just need to get together with a group of strangers and...
transcript: This is one of the most unique theatrical experiences I have ever had. It is part play and also part interactive game, where you and the rest of the audience are building a community together. Before the show starts, you choose a character. So, of course, I had to go with the Broadway baby. How much you choose to play into that character is completely up to you. Personally, I found it really fun to just lean into the character that you are given. And if you're feeling really ambitious, you can even run for mayor of the town. But the main activity of the show is voting for which projects you want the town to build. And voting coalitions formed very quickly. However, the mayor ultimately gets final say, and the winning project is then built in front of you out of food by the three main actors. Now, try as I might, every single round, I could not get a theater to be built. Even when our mayor was supposed to be an arts advocate, she still chose to build the farmers market instead. So I had to take matters into my own hands. I did run for mayor and was elected. And use the power entrusted to me by the will of the people to essentially force them to build a theater. But again, how much you choose to participate is completely optional, and I think this play works just as well if you are sitting in The corner and letting other people do the voting. Because it's not really about what gets built. It's about our voting processes and how those can get corrupted. And so, not only is it incredibly fun and silly and goofy, it also becomes a microcosm of society at large. And, yes, once it was over, we were given the option to eat the town that we just built. And you know what? It was delicious.
showTitle: Paradise Club Presents: Salvage City Supper Club
classificationReason: Creator attended and describes a unique interactive theatrical experience involving character selection, mayor elections, town-building votes, and food-based construction by three actors — closely matching the Salvage City Supper Club format. First-hand account with personal opinions ('one of the most unique theatrical experiences I have ever had').
